# MockForge

> MockForge is an open-source API mocking framework that simulates real backend behavior across HTTP/REST, gRPC, GraphQL, WebSockets, SMTP, and more. Point it at an OpenAPI spec, protobuf, or GraphQL schema and it serves realistic responses with intelligent synthetic data, stateful scenarios, and failure injection. MIT or Apache-2.0 licensed, with an optional cloud offering for hosted mocks.

## When to use MockForge

- You are developing or testing against a backend API that is unfinished, unstable, rate-limited, or expensive to call, and you need a faithful stand-in.
- You want contract testing: serve mocks generated directly from an OpenAPI spec (or protobuf / GraphQL schema) so clients fail fast when the contract drifts.
- You need to exercise failure paths: latency, errors, malformed responses, rate limits, and chaos scenarios that a real staging environment won't reproduce on demand.
- You need deterministic synthetic test data (personas, pagination-aware lists, seeded fixtures) instead of hand-written JSON fixtures.
- You want to mock gRPC, GraphQL, WebSocket, Kafka, SMTP, or FTP services, not just REST.

## When NOT to use MockForge

- As a production API gateway or proxy — MockForge simulates services; it does not replace them in production traffic paths.
- As a general-purpose load-testing tool — use its bench tooling to generate load against targets, but it is not a SaaS load-testing platform.

## How an agent should use it

- Install the CLI (`cargo install mockforge-cli`, Homebrew, npm SDKs, or Docker) and run `mockforge http --spec <openapi-file>` to serve a mock from an OpenAPI spec. See https://docs.mockforge.dev for all protocols and flags.
- The admin UI runs by default; every behavior is also scriptable over HTTP and config files (`mockforge.yaml`), so agents can drive it without a browser.
- Config is declarative: generate or edit a `mockforge.yaml` rather than clicking through the UI.

## API

- MockForge Cloud API (live): https://registry.mockforge.dev — auth, API tokens, organizations, marketplace, hosted mocks, billing. OpenAPI spec: https://mockforge.dev/openapi.registry.json
- Live demo instance (no signup): https://api.mockforge.dev — a real MockForge server running the bundled example specs (ecommerce store, weather, chat). Mock endpoints are callable directly; the management API lets you create and modify mocks at runtime. Management API spec: https://mockforge.dev/openapi.json
- The management API (mounted at `/__mockforge/api` on any MockForge server, including the demo) lets agents create, update, and delete mocks over HTTP — no browser or UI required.

## Contact

- Security issues: security@mockforge.dev (please do not open public issues for vulnerabilities)
- Bugs and features: https://github.com/SaaSy-Solutions/mockforge/issues
